device.model: TurtleBot3 Waffle Pi in Gazebo with GMAPPING and RRT exploration
device.name: ros_autonomous_slam TurtleBot3 exploration stack

facts.text: The README describes a ROS package that uses the Navigation Stack, GMAPPING and a Gazebo TurtleBot3 Waffle Pi to explore an unknown environment and build a map.
The autonomous explorer launch includes the SLAM launch, the turtlebot3_navigation move_base launch and the selected explorer launch.
The RRT launch passes /map as map_topic to both RRT detectors and to filter.py, and passes /filtered_points as frontiers_topic to assigner.py.
The RRT explorer imports nav_msgs/Odometry and nav_msgs/OccupancyGrid.
The RRT explorer subscribes to the absolute /odom and /map topics with those message types.
filter.py imports the package's PointArray message from ros_autonomous_slam.msg.
filter.py creates a PointArray publisher on the relative topic 'filtered_points' with queue size 10.
PointArray.msg defines the message as an array of geometry_msgs/Point named points.
filter.py appends the clustered centroids to arraypoints and publishes the PointArray on filterpub.
assigner.py subscribes to frontiers_topic as a PointArray.
The assigner sends the winning centroid with robots[id_record[winner_id]].sendGoal.
wall_follow.py creates a LaserScan subscriber on the absolute /scan topic and a Twist publisher on the absolute /cmd_vel topic.
wall_follow.py copies the LaserScan ranges into x and loops over 360 bins.
After its control loop exits, wall_follow.py publishes a zero Twist and prints 'Turtlebot stopped'.
The RRT explorer creates an actionlib SimpleActionClient for move_base and sends a MoveBaseGoal; this is an internal navigation call, not an upstream command server.
The README tells the operator to define the exploration region with boundary and start points using the RVIZ Publish Points option.
The global RRT detector subscribes to the absolute /clicked_point topic.
The global RRT detector includes geometry_msgs/PointStamped.h.
The global RRT detector waits until five clicked points have been collected, then uses points 0, 2 and 4 as the region corners and start point.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned responses with no physics step, pacing or state-hash replay; the same placeholder messages are returned on every subscription

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free canned transport: it answers the declared /map, /filtered_points, /odom and /scan subscriptions and runs no Gazebo physics, GMAPPING, SLAM, RRT, wall-following, TF, move_base or wall-clock loop
all map, frontier, odometry and scan values are placeholders and do not establish a trajectory, sensor frame, collision state or timing

the fake returns a 4 by 3 map with 12 occupancy cells and 3 frontier points; the live map size is the OccupancyGrid width times height and the live frontier count is the filtered cluster count, neither of which is fixed by the clone

the fake returns 8 LaserScan ranges; wall_follow.py loops over 360 bins (wall_follow.py:36-37) and the RRT nodes allocate 384 by 384 map buffers (autonomous_rrt.py:24), but these are code assumptions, not a universal live array size

the upstream publishes /cmd_vel internally and calls the external /move_base action; this package does not bind either as a command and does not simulate motion, navigation, a stop service or an emergency stop

the /clicked_point observation shows one operator point at a time; the RRT detectors accumulate five points in order (src/global_rrt_detector.cpp:132-175), and this package does not publish them or start exploration
the upstream filtered_points message has no header, so the frontiers observation carries no sample time
no world step, reset, snapshot, Gazebo service, ROS graph, TF or QoS configuration is exposed or validated; the operator runs the upstream nodes and rosbridge separately

the bridge refuses non-finite JSON numbers, so a live LaserScan whose ranges carry a no-return value encoded as a non-finite number fails the scan observation instead of returning it; the fake publishes finite placeholder ranges except in its non-finite test case

every observation subscribes with the 2 s wire default; /clicked_point is published only when an operator publishes a point in RViz (README.md:34-35), so that read fails unless a point arrives within 2 s
messages are bounded by the 1 MiB rosbridge default; a live OccupancyGrid whose JSON exceeds it is refused, not truncated, and the clone does not fix the live map size

measures.description: Read one fresh nav_msgs/OccupancyGrid publication from the exploration stack's /map topic.
measures.name: read_occupancy_map

measures.description: Read one fresh PointArray of clustered frontier targets from /filtered_points.
measures.name: read_frontiers

measures.description: Read one fresh operator-published geometry_msgs/PointStamped from /clicked_point. The RRT detectors accumulate five such points; this action shows one point and does not publish the region or start exploration.
measures.name: read_exploration_region

measures.description: Read one fresh nav_msgs/Odometry publication from the exploration stack's /odom topic.
measures.name: read_odometry

measures.description: Read one fresh sensor_msgs/LaserScan publication from the exploration stack's /scan topic.
measures.name: read_scan

safe_state.description: No actuation is bound: the upstream nodes publish /cmd_vel and call the external /move_base action internally, while this package only subscribes to /map, /filtered_points, /clicked_point, /odom and /scan, so an e-stop is the runtime software latch and no physical safe state is claimed.
